title: Mitigate hot-tenant join bloat via hash-prefixing and online remap
creator: Maya Alvarez
description: Problem: A small fraction of tenants drive very large join fanout across control-plane tables (projects, refs, audit_events). These hot-tenants cause wide table scans, inflated join costs, and frequent bloat that increases IO and query CPU. We've observed repeated spikes in PG cpu_percent and p99 control-plane API latency attributable to joins on tenant_id + legacy_lookup_key patterns. Goal: introduce a non-breaking, low-lock technique to spread tenant lookup entropy and reduce per-tenant index bloat without a long downtime or heavy coordinator locks.
motivation: Reduce p99 API latency under heavy multi-tenant workloads, shrink index sizes for the worst 1% of tenants by >=50%, and remove a source of VACUUM churn. Make indexing strategy more robust to skewed tenant traffic while preserving API compatibility and query semantics.
acceptance_criteria: New hash-prefix column exists and is populated for >= 99% of rows with background backfill
Queries that previously used tenant_id + legacy_lookup_key are rewritten to use (tenant_hash_prefix, tenant_id) and demonstrate >=30% reduction in median cost on profiled problematic tenants
Index footprint for top-1% tenants reduced by >=50% in production after compaction runs
No more than 1% increase in overall write latency during the backfill window (measured by control-plane ingest p95)
Rollback path verified: feature flag toggles queries back to old path within 5 minutes with no data loss
migration_plan: 1) Add new column tenant_hash_prefix (smallint) with default 0, nullable true. 2) Deploy query-layer change gated behind feature flag 'hash_pref_join' so read paths can use the new composite index when present but fall back to legacy plan. 3) Start asynchronous backfill job (kafka -> worker) that computes hash_prefix = (xxhash64(tenant_id) >> 48) & 0xFFFF for batches of tenant ranges; job emits progress to metrics and checkpoint in controlplane_migration_progress table. 4) After backfill reaches 99% rows and compaction window, create partial indexes per-shard using (tenant_hash_prefix, tenant_id, legacy_lookup_key) with INCLUDE for commonly selected columns. 5) Gradually enable feature flag for 5%/25%/100% traffic ramp. 6) Run targeted VACUUM+REINDEX for affected tables and monitor bloat metrics for two weeks. 7) Remove legacy indexes once stability and size goals met.
rollback_plan: 1) Toggle feature flag off to restore legacy query plans immediately. 2) Stop backfill workers; leave tenant_hash_prefix column alone (safe to keep). 3) If an index creation caused issues, drop the newly created index. 4) If partial compaction caused unexpected regressions, revert aggressive VACUUM(REINDEX) steps and open incident runbook. 5) Document residual column as low-risk technical debt to be addressed in next cycle.
rollout_strategy: Canary-by-tenant: enable hash_pref_join for internal admin tenants and non-critical customers, then progressively expand to groups using the console rollout tool. Each step validated by synthetic traffic replay and real traffic A/B for 24h with automated rollback if p95 API latency increases >8% or error rate >0.5% above baseline.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Backfill throttles DB and increases write latency. Mitigation: backfill workers respect DB connection pool and use small batches; micro-sleep between batches and adaptive concurrency based on recent p95 writes.

Risk: Query planner chooses suboptimal plans when both indexes exist. Mitigation: add planner hints in the ORM layer under feature flag; coordinate with PG tuning team to test on perf cluster before wide rollout.
Risk: Partial index creation fails due to table bloat. Mitigation: sequence index creation during low-traffic maintenance windows and rely on CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY where possible.
Risk: Operator error during reindexing. Mitigation: pre-populated runbook and automated scripts with dry-run steps and idempotent checks.
Risk: Unforeseen interaction with Dedicated control-plane tenants. Mitigation: coordinate a pre-rollout meeting with Dedicated PM and SRE; schedule separate windows for Dedicated customers.
Risk: Observability blind spots. Mitigation: create dashboards (sql-plan-diff, per-tenant-index-size, backfill-progress) and alert thresholds before enabling flags.

notes: Initial profiling (2026-01) showed that 0.8% of tenants were responsible for 42% of join CPU in projects->refs->audit_events joins.
We considered sharding by tenant_id modulo N but rejected due to large-scale refactor and migration complexity across multiple lookup tables.
Hash-prefix approach provides a stable, backward-compatible column that increases selectivity for indexes and can be rolled out without a global re-shard.
We will keep tenant_hash_prefix nullable during rollout to preserve compatibility with older rows and allow safe incremental backfill.
Estimate assumes CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY available in our PG version; if not, we will add short maintenance windows per table.
Coordinate with Security for helm values if backfill workers require new KMS scopes (unlikely).
